hints: Look first at what particles make up ammonium carbonate, it is a salt made from positive and negative ions.
Recall how an $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion forms when ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, gains an $\text{H}^+$ ion.
Check inside both ions for shared electrons, then check between the ions for attraction, to decide if all three bond types appear.
walkthrough:
**Spot the ions present**

Think of ammonium carbonate as separate ions packed together, not as single molecules.

$$ (\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{CO}_3^{2-} $$

**Bonding inside the ammonium ion**

In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen already has three normal covalent N-H bonds plus a lone pair. That lone pair is donated to $\text{H}^+$ to make $\text{NH}_4^+$.

$$ \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+ $$
This means $\text{NH}_4^+$ contains both normal covalent bonds and one co-ordinate (dative covalent) N to H bond.

**Bonding inside the carbonate ion**

In $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$, carbon and oxygen atoms share electrons. These are strong covalent bonds holding the polyatomic ion together.

**Bonding between the ions**

The positive $\text{NH}_4^+$ ions and the negative $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ion attract each other electrostatically. This is ionic bonding.

So 1 (ionic), 2 (covalent) and 3 (co-ordinate) are all present.

options.A: Correct. Ionic bonding acts between $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$, covalent bonding holds C to O in carbonate and N to H in ammonium, and co-ordinate bonding is present where N donates its lone pair to $\text{H}^+$ to form $\text{NH}_4^+$. So 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes ionic and covalent but leaves out co-ordinate bonding. Many students forget that $\text{NH}_4^+$ must contain a dative bond from nitrogen to the fourth hydrogen.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes covalent and co-ordinate but leaves out ionic. It is a trap if you focus only inside the ions and forget the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ions.
options.D: Incorrect. This is ionic only. It correctly spots the salt character but ignores all the strong covalent and dative bonds that hold the polyatomic ions themselves together.
